info.name: Integration API V2
info.description: Option B bidirectional contract. A V2 API key selected at key creation is required. The partner owns durable permit-package storage; BPH provides one-hour signed URLs and supports re-GET for refreshed URLs. Ingest on `permit_application_package_ready`, not on `permit_application_status_changed`. Submitting a meeting request emits `project_meeting_requested`. Fetch it at `GET /external_api/v2/project_meetings/{id}` and accept an open request with `PATCH /external_api/v2/project_meetings/{id}`. Partners write canonical application statuses and project state and are authoritative; manual-status conflict UX is deferred.

item.name: Permit applications
item.description: Application statuses: `new_draft` (Draft), `newly_submitted` (Submitted), `in_review` (In review), `revisions_requested` (Revisions requested), `resubmitted` (Resubmitted), `approved` (Approved), `issued` (Issued), `withdrawn` (Withdrawn). Partner-writable statuses: `in_review`, `approved`, `issued`, `withdrawn`, `revisions_requested`.

request.description: Slim application resource: identity and submission version index. Does not include submission_data or zip files.

Frozen submission snapshot for one version, including form data, generated PDFs, zipfile (File object, null if that version never received a zip), and signed file URLs. Ingest after permit_application_package_ready. URLs expire in one hour; re-GET to refresh.

Uses canonical BPH status codes. Lifecycle transitions are enforced and repeated writes of the current status are idempotent. For `revisions_requested`, send a non-empty `revision_requests` array of field-level items (`requirement_block_code`, `requirement_code`, `reason_code`, `comment`) copied from the submission version payload. `revision_requests` must be omitted for every other status. Invalid, reserved, or unavailable transitions return 422 naming the statuses available from the current status.

One-call revision request: creates field-level revision requests on the latest submission version and moves the application to `revisions_requested`, notifying the submitter. Target fields with `requirement_block_code` + `requirement_code` from GET submission version. Reason codes come from GET /revision_reasons.

item.name: Get Integration Mapping by Version ID
Permit projects
item.description: Project GET follows `permit_project_id` from application reads and webhooks. Child summaries omit drafts and include `revisions_requested`. PATCH state accepts only `available_states` from the current state. Collaborators, notes, and project documents stay in BPH. Fetch and accept meeting requests from the Project meetings folder.

request.description: Non-draft projects in the key's jurisdiction and sandbox, the same set as the jurisdiction inbox with no filters. Optional constraints.state narrows to one non-draft state. draft is ignored.
Project identity, state, available_states, address, and sibling application summaries (id, number, status, status_label, tags).

Sets project state to a code in `available_states` for the current state. `draft` is not a partner write. Writing the current state returns 200 and does not emit another `permit_project_state_changed`. Illegal or unknown codes return 422 and name the available states.

item.name: Revision reasons
item.description: Site-configured revision reason codes. The list is dynamic; do not hard-code a static enum.

request.description: Kept (non-discarded) reason codes accepted on revision_requests.

item.name: Project meetings
item.description: GET a submitted meeting request, including one-hour signed document URLs. PATCH accepts an open request by scheduling it. Drafts are not readable.

request.description: Contact, description, property-information flag, project identity, and meeting_request_documents with signed download URLs. A later GET returns new URLs.

Schedules an open meeting. contact_method is phone, in_person, or videoconference. meeting_url is required for videoconference and must be an http(s) URL when present. Success returns status scheduled and sends the existing scheduled notifications. A meeting that is not open returns 422.

item.name: Webhook events

request.description: Development only. Point a V2 key webhook URL at this same address, then GET it to see the last deliveries.

item.description: V2 emits `permit_application_status_changed` for each externally visible application status transition, including submission and resubmission. Payload: `{ permit_application_id, permit_project_id, submission_version_id, status, status_label, occurred_at }`. Durable ingest waits for `permit_application_package_ready` (`{ permit_application_id, permit_project_id, submission_version_id, number, reference_number, occurred_at }`), which fires once per submission version after generated PDFs exist and the application zip is rebuilt. V2 also emits `permit_project_state_changed` with `{ permit_project_id, state, state_label, occurred_at }`. Project states: `draft` (Draft), `queued` (Queued), `waiting` (Waiting), `in_progress` (In progress), `ready` (Ready), `permit_issued` (Permit issued), `active` (Active), `complete` (Completed), `closed` (Closed). Submitting a meeting request emits `project_meeting_requested` with `{ project_meeting_id, permit_project_id, status, occurred_at }` and no file URL, even when the project has no submitted permit application. Timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds. All bodies use the `{ event, payload }` envelope and `X-Webhook-Signature` HMAC-SHA256 header. File URLs are not included in webhooks; fetch them after package_ready, or from GET project meeting for meeting documents. In development, set the key webhook URL to `{{webhook_url}}`.
